description.narrative: Gender Barriers: Young women in Eastern Samar face significant obstacles to employment due to entrenched gender biases in hiring practices, societal expectations that restrict their workforce participation, and stereotypes that discourage them from pursuing careers in high-demand sectors like green jobs and STEM fields. The root causes include persistent cultural norms, unequal distribution of domestic responsibilities, and undervaluing of women’s contributions in the economy. Regional Vulnerability: Eastern Samar’s location exposes it to frequent natural disasters such as typhoons, floods, landslides, and earthquakes—problems exacerbated by climate change. These recurring hazards regularly disrupt livelihoods, education, and essential government services, undermining long-term development. The root cause is the province’s geographic position and inadequate infrastructure to withstand environmental shocks. Economic Challenges for Youth: Youth unemployment in Eastern Samar is high, with limited opportunities outside agriculture, fisheries, and informal sectors. Many young people have restricted access to quality education or technical-vocational training, resulting in a workforce that lacks skills for stable, well-paid jobs. The underlying reasons include insufficient educational institutions, inadequate resources for training, and a mismatch between market needs and youth qualifications.

Plan International Pilipinas will leverage on its youth economic empowerment initiatives in Eastern Samar to enhance sustainability beyond the project. With strong local partnerships, the program connects youth with training, industry, and government support to boost employability and financial access. Digital and green skills curricula are featured, benefiting both current and future programs. The alumni network, supported via a safeguarded Facebook hub, is youth-led and vital for sustainability, expanding project impact beyond 5,300 beneficiaries through advocacy and peer engagement. Collaboration with employers ensures training aligns with market needs, increasing job prospects for youth and fostering ongoing opportunities. By leveraging partnerships and empowering young people, the project creates lasting pathways towards economic inclusion and resilience.

Plan International will focus on overcoming the economic barriers that youth face by enhancing their access to decent work and entrepreneurship opportunities. The following outcomes are aimed: 1. Youth equipped with foundational and entrepreneurship skills, knowledge and mindset to improve their career development and potential for (self)employment 2. Youth build social connections and networks that enable support for their (economic) development 3. Youth pursue decent work opportunities of their choosing in the twin green and digital transition Through these efforts, Plan International aims to break the cycle of poverty by providing young people with the tools they need to achieve economic success, while also tackling broader social issues such as inequality and limited access to education.
Supporting elements of the project includes marker scan of green training and job opportunities; technical working group with partners agencies and alumni & peer mentorship networks. As cross-cutting interventions, the project will build on Plan international’s gender transformative and inclusion principles; meaning youth engagement and climate and disaster resilience experience.

SUMMARY: Between October 2024 and May 2027 the Twin transition project aims to empower 5,300 young people, particularly young women in all their diversity, in Eastern Samar (Philippines) with life skills, digital skills, and green life skills to improve access to and participation in the labour market in the green and digital sectors. Through training, digital tools, and improved access to social programs and networks, 15-30-year-olds not in education, employment or training (NEET) benefit from support, knowledge, and opportunities they need to build sustainable livelihoods and achieve economic independence. Additionally, young people will enjoy enhanced access to employment and entrepreneurial opportunities in the green and digital sectors.Plan international will work together with governmental and private sector partners.

The Twin Transition project offers demand-driven, high-quality training and support to help young people, particularly young women, secure decent work and economic opportunities. The following activities will be conducted: Outcome 1: • Conduct a need and market assessment • Training for youth to develop life, green, entrepreneurship and technical skills • Enhancement of digital app Hope Town Hero to improve youth participation • Train the trainer for TVET and senior high school teachers on life, digital and green life skills Outcome 2: • Organize an alumni network of youth participants and technical working group • Facilitate access for youth to social connections and networks and campaigns • Community awareness campaigns • Facilitate youth, especially young women to pursue meaningful work opportunities of their choice Outcome 3: • Provision of financial support to young people for wage employment or set-up of a small business • Conduct of Special Recruitment Activity (SRA) and Livelihood Fair (Kabuhayan fair). • Young entrepreneurs training workshop

The project will focus on youth aged 15-30 not in education, employment or training (NEET), with 60% being young women, from low-income families, youth-led or elderly-led households, and young mothers or parents. The project will cover five (5) municipalities in Eastern Samar. The focus will be on individuals willing to be trained and seeking employment or looking to establish their own livelihoods. The project will also actively encourage the participation of youth from all backgrounds and with diverse sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics (SOGIESC). It will create an inclusive atmosphere so that every young person, regardless of identity or ability, has an equal opportunity to participate. The project will engage with 5 national high schools and 3 agricultural schools (TVIs) accredited by the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) and will train teachers with of these organisations with gender and green skills training so they can transfer their knowledge to their students.

Youth unemployment in the Philippines is shaped by structural, social, and economic factors. As of mid-2024, the rate stands at 6.7%, with young women disproportionately affected. Underemployment is high at 12.1%. A key issue is the mismatch between education and labour market needs, with outdated vocational training and limited practical skills. Gender disparities hinder employment, especially for young women and SOGIESC individuals, due to societal norms and biased hiring. The green and digital transitions offer opportunities, but youth face barriers to training and jobs. Eastern Samar highlights local challenges: isolation, frequent disasters, and poor infrastructure. Youth unemployment there exceeds 20%, with limited education and vocational resources. Gender inequalities are pronounced, with cultural expectations restricting women’s participation. Solutions require targeted interventions, investment in green and digital skills, and gender-responsive policies to empower youth and foster inclusive growth.
